headline: High: ECC’s default write/network/MCP surface can conflict with Botpress workflows and create cascading errors; compliance risk is lower but nonzero.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Botpress is a customer-support agent with no documented isolation or provenance controls, while ECC exposes MCP, stdin/stdout, and file surfaces that can ingest external content. If Botpress outputs are routed into ECC skills or MCP workflows, prompt-like content could be treated as instructions. The interaction is inferred from docs only, so uncertainty pushes this to medium.
conditions: IF Botpress outputs are copied into ECC prompts, skills, or MCP inputs
IF ECC processes Botpress-generated text as trusted instructions without provenance checks
mitigations: Disable automatic handoff from Botpress to ECC prompts
Add a manual review step before ECC executes Botpress text
Restrict ECC MCP servers to trusted sources only
Tag Botpress outputs as untrusted in the workflow
requires-engineering: add provenance filtering between agents

B_data_leakage.rationale: Botpress has network egress set to none, but ECC reads and writes local files, handles secrets, and can call external APIs. If both agents share a workspace or session files, Botpress content can be exposed to ECC and then to third-party services. The shared-workspace pathway is not explicitly documented, so this remains medium rather than high.
conditions: IF Botpress and ECC share any filesystem or session directory
IF ECC forwards shared file contents to GitHub, Supabase, Vercel, Railway, or Nutrient API
mitigations: Separate Botpress and ECC working directories
Move secrets out of shared folders
Disable ECC API calls for sensitive projects
Review ECC session files for leaked Botpress content
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent storage isolation

C_capability_conflict.rationale: ECC can execute shell commands, write files, and modify git state; Botpress can install packages. If both operate on the same repo or workspace, concurrent writes and package changes can overwrite each other or corrupt state. Because ECC explicitly supports multiple instances and shared-state warnings, the conflict is plausible in default developer setups and can cause irreversible repo damage.
conditions: IF Botpress and ECC target the same repository or filesystem root
IF package installation or git edits occur concurrently without locking
mitigations: Use separate repos or worktrees
Pause one agent before the other writes
Turn on file-locking around git operations
Keep package installs manual and serialized
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level concurrency locks

D_cascading_error.rationale: ECC’s workflow surface is built around skills, hooks, and subagents, so it can readily act on upstream text. Botpress is a support bot that may generate user-facing content; if ECC consumes that output as authoritative, mistakes can cascade into commits, API calls, or other actions. The pairwise pathway is inferred, but the downstream action authority makes the blast radius high.
conditions: IF ECC uses Botpress output as source material for skills or hooks
IF ECC is allowed to execute shell, git, or API actions based on that output
mitigations: Require human approval before ECC acts on Botpress output
Add verification against source documents before execution
Limit ECC to read-only mode for Botpress-derived tasks
Log and diff all Botpress-to-ECC handoffs
requires-engineering: implement output validation gates

E_compliance.rationale: Botpress is open-source with no stated residency or retention controls, while ECC explicitly stores session summaries, metrics, hooks, and retention-related secrets. If the pair processes regulated data, the mismatch in retention and storage behavior can create compliance gaps. The other agent is cited because the risk arises from their combined handling of the same data class.
conditions: IF regulated data is processed through both agents
IF ECC retention settings or session files retain data longer than Botpress workflows expect
mitigations: Avoid regulated data in shared workflows
Set ECC retention to the minimum practical value
Review which session fields are persisted
Document data-flow ownership for both agents
requires-engineering: align retention and residency controls
